Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Sunil Kumar Yadav,Yashpal Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
340 of 2023 at Police Station Jansath, District Muzaffarnagar under Sections 452, 354Kha, 376 I.P.C.
The applicant is in jail since 29.12.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 14.02.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Sunil Kumar Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Shravan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1. The applicant and the victim reside in the same neighbourhood.
2. The FIR is a result of a neighbourhood dispute between the parties.
3. The applicant was falsely implicated only to leverage the criminal case in the said neighbourhood dispute and blackmail the applicant.

4. No allegation of commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has been made in the FIR or in the statement of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
5.
The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has completely denied the prosecution case and has asserted that the applicant did not molest or act inappropriately with her.

6. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
discredit the prosecution case.
7. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
8. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Malkit be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
